what: joining a body with an internal modelled thread to one with an external modelled thread, touching in a plane (the join ran for over ten minutes)
method: ISO 68-1 basic profile: H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8. External groove (the space between teeth): a trapezoid P/4 wide at the root radius d/2 - 5H/8, widening by 2 tan30 per unit of radius to 7P/8 at d/2. Internal groove: P/8 wide at the major radius d/2, widening to 3P/4 at the minor radius, cut only where there is material (r >= hole radius). Pappus: volume per turn = 2 pi A rc (A the trapezoid area, rc its centroid radius from the axis); a helical sweep of L/P turns removes exactly (L/P) x that, where each end of the thread is a free end or lies inside material. A as in the one-body case (V_A = 8400.9644). B: cylinder R=13.05 h=14 with M26.1x1.814 over its whole length, both ends free: V_B = pi 13.05^2 14 - (14/1.814) x 79.63016 = 6875.7294. They touch only in the plane z=12 (B's flat end on A's flat top), so the join is one solid with V = V_A + V_B = 15276.6938 mm3. Tolerance 1%: a modelled thread is a faceted helical solid (radial chord error up to 1% of the pitch on every wall, i.e. a volume deficit of about 4/3 x sag/R).
